CFML Language Reference: Functions

QueryNew

Creates a new query object with the columns you name and no rows. You can then fill it and use it anywhere a CFQUERY result works: CFOUTPUT QUERY, CFLOOP QUERY, CFTABLE, ValueList and so on.

Category

Query functions

Syntax

QueryNew(columnlist)

Parameters

columnlist
A comma-separated list of column names. Spaces around the names are ignored. An empty string gives a query with no columns, to which you can add columns with QueryAddColumn.

Returns

An empty query. Its RecordCount is 0 and its ColumnList holds the column names in uppercase.

Usage

Hand-made queries are a convenient way to hold tabular data that does not come from a database, such as the result of parsing a text file. Remember that queries, like structures, are passed by reference; use Duplicate for a private copy.

Example

Opens the example in a new window. The example runs on this server, so it only works when you browse from the server itself (127.0.0.1).
<CFSET Modems = QueryNew("Speed, Year")>
<CFSET Temp = QueryAddRow(Modems, 3)>
<CFSET Temp = QuerySetCell(Modems, "Speed", "14.4K", 1)>
<CFSET Temp = QuerySetCell(Modems, "Year", 1991, 1)>
<CFSET Temp = QuerySetCell(Modems, "Speed", "28.8K", 2)>
<CFSET Temp = QuerySetCell(Modems, "Year", 1994, 2)>
<CFSET Temp = QuerySetCell(Modems, "Speed", "56K", 3)>
<CFSET Temp = QuerySetCell(Modems, "Year", 1998, 3)>

<CFOUTPUT><P>RecordCount: #Modems.RecordCount#, ColumnList: #Modems.ColumnList#</P></CFOUTPUT>
<TABLE BORDER=1 CELLPADDING=3>
<TR><TH>Speed</TH><TH>Year</TH></TR>
<CFOUTPUT QUERY="Modems">
<TR><TD>#Speed#</TD><TD>#Year#</TD></TR>
</CFOUTPUT>
</TABLE>
